name: How often elevators must be inspected in each US state: intervals, filing rules, fees and the ASME A17.1 edition enforced
description: Per-state elevator inspection requirements: how often a passenger elevator must be inspected, who performs and files the inspection, the filing fee and deadline, the penalty for a missed inspection, and which edition of the ASME A17.1 safety code the state enforces. The variation is large: Texas requires inspection every 12 months with the report and $20-per-unit fee filed to TDLR within 30 days, and administrative penalties up to $5,000 per day for missed inspections (Texas Health & Safety Code ch. 754); New York City tests twice annually with a Category 5 load test every five years; the enforced A17.1 edition spans roughly 2004 (California) to 2019 (Connecticut). Answers 'how often does my building's elevator need to be inspected?', 'what happens if the elevator inspection is late?', 'which ASME A17.1 edition does my state enforce?'
licence: Sources are US state and city government pages (public records). We take facts plus short attributed quotes linking back. ASME A17.1 itself is a standards-reseller document: we record which edition a state enforces (a fact about the state's law), never the standard's content.

records.inspection_interval: inspected at least once each year
records.who_inspects: the division shall cause all conveyances to be inspected
records.source_quote: (a) Except as provided in subdivision (b), the division shall cause all conveyances to be inspected at least once each year. If a conveyance is found upon inspection to be in a safe condition for operation, a permit for operation for not longer than one year shall be issued by the division. (b) If a conveyance is subject to a full maintenance service contract, the division may, after investigation and inspection, issue a permit for operation for not longer than two years.

records.who_inspects: a certified elevator inspector or by a municipality or county under contract with the division
records.penalty: the division may seal the elevator or order the discontinuance of the use of the elevator
records.source_quote: All elevators or other conveyances subject to this chapter must be annually inspected by a certified elevator inspector or by a municipality or county under contract with the division

records.who_inspects: an approved elevator agency on behalf of the owner
records.filing_rule: Periodic inspections must be submitted within 14 days of inspection date to avoid late fees
records.penalty: Filings not submitted by January 14 of the following year will not be accepted and failure to file violations will be issued
records.source_quote: In accordance with the NYC Building Codes, elevators must be inspected and tested twice annually. The periodic inspection is performed by an approved elevator agency on behalf of the owner. The agency performing the periodic inspection cannot be affiliated with the agency performing maintenance on the device. Periodic Inspection An annual visual inspection performed between January 1 and December 31. Periodic inspections must be submitted within 14 days of inspection date to avoid late fees. Filings not submitted by January 14 of the following year will not be accepted and failure to file violations will be issued.

records.filing_rule: submit the inspection report, all required documents, and applicable fees to the Department
records.penalty: civil penalties up to $5,000 per day for each violation
records.authority: Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation
records.statute: Texas Health and Safety Code, Chapter 754
records.source_quote: The owner of the elevator or related equipment must obtain an inspection every 12 months and submit the inspection report, all required documents, and applicable fees to the Department in order to obtain a Certificate of Compliance.

records.inspection_interval: inspected and tested at least once each year
records.who_inspects: The department shall appoint and employ inspectors
records.penalty: A penalty may be assessed under RCW 70.87.185 for failure to correct a violation within ninety days after the owner is notified in writing of inspection results
records.source_quote: Except as provided in (b) of this subsection, the department shall cause all conveyances to be inspected and tested at least once each year. Inspectors have the right during reasonable hours to enter into and upon any building or premises in the discharge of their official duties, for the purpose of making any inspection or testing any conveyance contained thereon or therein. Inspections and tests shall conform with the rules adopted by the department. The department shall inspect all installations before it issues any initial permit for operation. Permits shall not be issued until the fees required by this chapter have been paid.
